SenseDetailRead.description:
The full lexical record for one sense, returned by the single-sense read
alone. Listing endpoints return ``SenseContent`` so their payload does not
grow.
SenseDetailRead.title: SenseDetailRead

SenseFormRead.description:
One inflected form: ``surface`` (ran) tagged with its ``inf`` label (past).

Field names mirror Lexi's ``FormView`` exactly. Do not rename them to anything
resembling an answer-key shape: ``test_v1_contract`` substring-scans the whole
component-schema document for the three answer-safety tokens, so even prose in
a docstring here can trip it.
SenseFormRead.title: SenseFormRead

SenseRelationRead.description:
A sense-level semantic relation. ``wsdState`` is derived by Lexi, not
stored: ``resolved`` carries a target sense, ``pending`` and ``unresolvable``
carry only the target word.
SenseRelationRead.title: SenseRelationRead

SessionSenseProgressRead.description: Where one admitted sense stands. Live-session shape only.
SessionSenseProgressRead.title: SessionSenseProgressRead

SessionStateRead.description:
One session, live or finished.

``status`` discriminates: ``live`` is served from Redis and carries the round
counters and per-sense progress; ``completed`` is served from the durable
summary row and carries the recap counts only, because ``end_session`` deleted
the live namespace. A client that reloads mid-session gets ``live``; one that
reloads after finishing gets ``completed`` instead of a 404.
SessionStateRead.title: SessionStateRead

ViewerRead.description:
The ``GET /v1/me`` projection.

Exists so ``token_version`` cannot reach the browser. It was previously served
because ``CurrentUser`` doubled as the response model, which meant the
revocation counter shipped to every client that asked who it was.
ViewerRead.title: ViewerRead

WeakSenseRead.description:
A weakest-sense row. Carries enough to render without a second request:
the previous shape was ``{senseId, mastery}``, which is a progress bar with no
label.
WeakSenseRead.title: WeakSenseRead

Resolved through the planner's own reader, so a deck with no settings row — or

get.description:
List the caller's roots or one owned folder's immediate children.

Public nodes deliberately have no discovery/listing surface; a public item is
visible only through an explicit direct link or a tree owned by its author.
Read a node directly; anonymous callers see public nodes only.

The full lexical record for one sense, authorized owner-or-public.

A sense is not an owned resource in pycil — it is Lexi content that becomes
reachable by being a member of a deck. So access is derived: the caller may
read the sense if at least one deck holding it is readable by them, which is
the same rule ``require_node_access`` applies to the deck itself.

Unknown, unreferenced and unreadable all return one 404 with one code, so the
endpoint cannot be used to probe which senses exist or who has them.

Read one session. A TRUE read — it advances nothing and reserves nothing.

Unlike ``/next``, which is a mutation dressed as a GET (it advances rounds,
reserves deliveries and extends the exclusion set), this endpoint is safe to
poll, retry and prefetch.

Live sessions are served from Redis. Once a session completes, ``end_session``
has deleted that namespace, so the durable recap answers instead. 404 only when
neither exists.
